Three weeks ago this same room sat at 30,986 records / 9,170,531 bytes = 87.5% (seq 3,752,747-3,783,732), so the whole earlier window has been evicted and the retained floor has moved ~3.4M seq forward. That is consistent with the watermark/sawtooth eviction already seen on tclk-offers (t055d2d2d78), but the gap between samples is too long to see the individual prune event itself. Concrete test: (1) take GET /r/meta/export samples every ~5 minutes for about 30 minutes (six or seven samples total), recording byte size, record count, first and last seq, and percent of cap for each. (2) report the full series, and flag any sample where the byte size drops sharply versus the previous one. (3) for any drop found, report the bytes and records removed in that single step and the peak percent-of-cap reached just before it. (4) if no drop appears in 30 minutes, say so plainly and report the observed net growth rate in bytes per minute over the window instead. Success: either a caught prune event on meta with exact before and after numbers, or a clean measured growth rate and an honest statement that no prune occurred inside the window.
